text.p: State-run Lithuanian Airlines said on Wednesday that its first quarter 1997 profit rose to 695,000 litas compared to losses of 812,000 litas for the same period last year.

"The company had a profit of 695,000 litas during the first three months of 1997 compared to 812,000 litas in losses in the first quarter of 1996," Bronius Jiechius, the company's finance and economy director, told Reuters.
"Our profit was up because we increased our passenger and cargo numbers," Jiecius added.
He said that the company served 38,400 passengers in the first quarter of 1997 versus 36,100 passengers last year.
He also said that the company transported 471 tonnes of cargo during the first three months of this year compared to 374 tonnes in the same period last year.
"Last December we leased a SAAB 340 B plane for short routes and it reduced our expenditures by nearly three times," Jiechius said.
The Lithuanian government plans to privatise Lithuanian Airlines in open bids in the next two years.
